interpretation.concurrent_measurement: Each concurrent batch (different-ref, cross-repo new pack, competing same-ref) is bracketed by exactly one measure()/scrape pair. Per-push worker wall times are reported separately and are not phase attributed, so concurrent phase deltas are never divided, summed or compared per push.
interpretation.historical_v1: Earlier v1 reports recorded one measure() per concurrent push. Those per-case phase deltas overlap in the process-global counters and are INVALID for individual or batch aggregation; they remain only as historical raw data. A v2 run replaces them.
interpretation.same_ref_rejection: The non-winning contender is classified as an observed HTTP409 conflict or a Git ref-rejection diagnostic (remote rejected / non-fast-forward / failed to update ref / stale info); an authentication or transport failure fails the run and is never counted as a ref rejection. This is ordinary competing pushes, not an explicit-old-OID CAS assertion.

scrape_overhead_ms.note: each scrape takes one pooled PostgreSQL connection and runs one SQL snapshot statement outside the instrumented spans, so before/after scrapes perturb the case slightly

phase_limits: Exact SQL lock wait is still unmeasured: state_row and authority_lock are client round trips and include statement submission, PostgreSQL execution and row return.
Values are per process. Counters reset across h.stop/h.start and are never differenced across processes; a case spanning a restart reports process_restarted instead of a delta.
Phase spans nest (native_git_hydration contains remote GET and decrypt) and must not be summed.
Bytes are logical payload of successful S3-backed transfers only; local-filesystem object storage emits no remote_* series, and retries, headers and TLS overhead are excluded.
